title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Lex Fridman Podcast #490 featuring Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discussing the current state of AI in 2026. Topics include Large Language Models, AI and Coding, Scaling Laws, China's AI developments, AI Agents, GPUs, and Artificial General Intelligence. The 4.5-hour conversation provides comprehensive insights into the current landscape and future directions of AI technology.
author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

title: Shadow APIs breaking research reproducibility crisis
description: A new paper (arxiv 2603.01919) audits shadow APIs - third party services claiming to provide GPT-5/Gemini access. Findings are alarming: 187 academic papers used these services, with the most popular one having 5,966 citations. Performance divergence up to 47%, safety behavior completely unpredictable, 45% of fingerprint tests failed identity verification. Many research papers might be built on fake model outputs. These services are popular due to payment barriers and regional restrictions. This undermines trust in the entire field and affects production systems that depend on specific model behavior.
author: Reddit r/MachineLearning community

title: Ads in AI Chatbots? An Analysis of How Large Language Models Navigate Conflicts of Interest
description: Research analyzing how LLMs handle conflicts of interest when ads are incorporated into AI chatbot interfaces. The study examines the implications for user trust and decision-making. This is relevant for AI coding tools that may include sponsored suggestions or recommendations.
author: Addison J. Wu, Ryan Liu, Shuyue Stella Li, et al.

title: SUPERNOVA: Eliciting General Reasoning in LLMs with Reinforcement Learning on Natural Instructions
description: New approach to improving general reasoning capabilities in LLMs using reinforcement learning on natural instructions. The 23-page paper with 4 figures presents a method for enhancing LLM reasoning without extensive supervised training. This could improve AI coding assistants' ability to reason about complex programming problems.
author: Ashima Suvarna, Kendrick Phan, Mehrab Beikzadeh, et al.

title: Verify Before You Commit: Towards Faithful Reasoning in LLM Agents via Self-Auditing
description: New research from ACL 2026 proposing a self-auditing framework for LLM agents to ensure faithful reasoning. The approach allows agents to verify their own reasoning before committing to actions, addressing reliability and trustworthiness concerns in agentic AI systems. This is particularly relevant for AI coding assistants that need to ensure code correctness before execution.
author: Wenhao Yuan, Chenchen Lin, Jian Chen, et al.

title: SkillClaw: Let Skills Evolve Collectively with Agentic Evolver
description: Novel framework for allowing skills in LLM agents to evolve collectively through an agentic evolver. The work in progress addresses the challenge of managing and improving tool-use capabilities in AI agents dynamically. This has implications for AI coding assistants that need to continuously improve their coding skills and tool usage.
author: Ziyu Ma, Shidong Yang, Yuxiang Ji, et al.

title: Beyond Stochastic Exploration: What Makes Training Data Valuable for Agentic Search
description: ACL 2026 Findings paper analyzing what makes training data valuable for agentic search systems. The 15-page paper provides insights into data curation for training better search-capable agents. This is relevant for improving AI coding assistants' ability to search through and understand codebases.
author: Chuzhan Hao, Wenfeng Feng, Guochao Jiang, et al.

title: PASK: Toward Intent-Aware Proactive Agents with Long-Term Memory
description: Technical report on proactive agents with intent-awareness and long-term memory capabilities. The framework enables agents to maintain context over extended interactions and take initiative based on inferred user intent. This is particularly relevant for AI coding assistants that need to remember project context and proactively suggest improvements.
author: Zhifei Xie, Zongzheng Hu, Fangda Ye, et al.

title: KnowU-Bench: Towards Interactive, Proactive, and Personalized Mobile Agent Evaluation
description: New benchmark for evaluating mobile AI agents with focus on interactivity, proactivity, and personalization. The benchmark addresses the unique challenges of agent behavior on mobile devices. This is relevant for evaluating AI coding assistants that run on mobile platforms or need to work across different devices.
author: Tongbo Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Zhan Xu, et al.

title: Lightweight LLM Agent Memory with Small Language Models
description: ACL 2026 accepted paper proposing using small language models to create lightweight memory systems for LLM agents. The approach addresses computational efficiency while maintaining effective memory capabilities for agentic systems. This has implications for making AI coding assistants more efficient and deployable.
author: Jiaquan Zhang, Chaoning Zhang, Shuxu Chen, et al.

title: SEARL: Joint Optimization of Policy and Tool Graph Memory for Self-Evolving Agents
description: ACL 2026 paper presenting a framework for self-evolving agents that jointly optimize policy and tool graph memory. The approach enables agents to continuously improve their tool-use strategies and adapt to new tasks. This has direct applications for AI coding assistants that need to learn and evolve their capabilities.
author: Xinshun Feng, Xinhao Song, Lijun Li, et al.

title: Fireship: The unhinged world of tech in 2026
description: Fireship's analysis of technology trends in 2026, covering AI, coding, and developer tools. The video with 1.4M views discusses the rapid evolution of the tech landscape and emerging patterns in software development.
author: Fireship

title: Fireship: 7 new open source AI tools you need right now
description: Fireship presents seven new open source AI coding tools and frameworks. The video covers practical tools for building meeting bots, desktop recording apps, and other AI-powered applications. Includes partnership content with Recall.ai about rapid AI development workflows.
author: Fireship

title: Meta's Muse Spark model and meta.ai chat tools
description: Meta announced Muse Spark, their first model release since Llama 4 almost exactly a year ago. It's hosted, not open weights, and the API is currently a private API preview to select users, but available to try on meta.ai (Facebook or Instagram login required). Simon Willison provides detailed analysis of the new model's capabilities and tools.
author: Simon Willison

title: GLM-5.1: Towards Long-Horizon Tasks - 754B parameter model
description: Chinese AI lab Z.ai's latest model is a giant 754B parameter 1.51TB MIT-licensed monster. Simon tested it with his 'pelican on a bicycle' SVG generation test. The model impressively generated both SVG and HTML with CSS animations. When the animation had bugs, the model correctly diagnosed the CSS transform issue and provided a fixed version. The model shows strong capabilities in understanding and debugging SVG/CSS interactions.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic's Project Glasswing - restricting Claude Mythos to security researchers
description: Anthropic didn't release their latest model, Claude Mythos, to the public. Instead, they made it available to a very restricted set of preview partners under their newly announced Project Glasswing. Simon discusses why this security-focused restricted access approach sounds necessary given the model's capabilities. The system card PDF provides details about the model's capabilities and safety considerations.
author: Simon Willison

title: Google AI Edge Gallery - running Gemma 4 models on iPhone
description: Google released an official app for running their Gemma 4 models (E2B and E4B sizes) directly on iPhone. The E2B model is a 2.54GB download, fast and genuinely useful. The app provides 'ask questions about images', audio transcription (up to 30s), and an interesting 'skills' demo demonstrating tool calling against eight different interactive widgets. This is the first time Simon has seen a local model vendor release an official iPhone app for trying out models.
author: Simon Willison

title: Hacker News: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026
description: Hacker News discussion about AI coding workflows and whether there's actually a speedup over doing coding yourself. The community debates the effectiveness of LLM-assisted programming and shares experiences about productivity gains versus overhead. Discussion highlights the nuanced reality of AI coding tools in practice.
author: Hacker News community

title: Hacker News: LLM coding workflow going into 2026
description: A developer's experience working on multi-step AI pipelines for 3D mesh generation, noting that LLMs often skip edge cases. The discussion explores the practical challenges of using LLMs for complex coding tasks and the importance of human oversight in catching edge cases that AI might miss.
author: Hacker News community

title: Hacker News: How would you learn to code in 2026?
description: Discussion about project-based learning approaches for coding in the current era. The community explores how learning to code has changed with AI assistance, shifting from memorizing syntax to verifying AI-generated work and understanding system architecture.
author: Hacker News community

title: Eight years of wanting, three months of building with AI - syntaqlite story
description: Lalit Maganti's long-form writing on agentic engineering: spent 8 years thinking about and 3 months building syntaqlite, high-fidelity devtools for SQLite. Key insights: AI helped overcome procrastination on tedious work (400+ grammar rules), but AI made design decisions harder - cheap refactoring led to deferred decisions that corroded clear thinking. The second attempt involved more human-in-the-loop design decisions. The article is full of non-obvious downsides to working heavily with AI and how to overcome them. Critical insight: 'When I was working on something where I didn't even know what I wanted, AI was somewhere between unhelpful and harmful.'
author: Simon Willison (citing Lalit Maganti)
